newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FORCE ZIMBABWE TO FOLLOW-ON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA FORCE ZIMBABWE TO FOLLOW-ON.

text.p: Sri Lanka forced Zimbabwe to
follow-on by dismissing them for 145 in their first innings but
their hopes of pressing home the advantage were hindered by rain
on the third day of the first test on Friday.
Intermittent showers, which washed out the first session of
play, returned 25 minutes before the scheduled tea break to
force the players off the ground.
Zimbabwe, following on 204 runs behind Sri Lanka's first
innings of 349, were 19 without loss at the interval.
Grant Flower was undefeated on 13 and Mark Dekker on six.
Left-arm spinner Jayantha Silva wrapped up the Zimbabwe
innings with two wickets off successive deliveries, putting
himself in line for a hat-trick in the Zimbabwe second innings.
Silva, who took just one wicket in his only previous test,
in Australia last year, finished with three for 10 off 14.5
overs, nine of which were maidens.
Resuming their first innings at 105 for six, Zimbabwe's last
four wickets added only 40 runs.
Only Craig Wishart stood firm against Sri Lanka's pace and
spin attack, scoring a resolute 51 in a stay of 205 minutes. He
faced 157 balls and hit one six and two fours.
Wishart miscued a drive to mid-off and off the next delivery
bowled after a 10-minute break for rain, Andrew Whittall pulled
a short delivery to Dharmasena at square leg.
Off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan took two for 28 off 24
overs and left-arm pace bowler Chaminda Vaas four for 73.
